land.text: Lusitania and Carthaginensis, where Respendial's Alans settled

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's first Alan shape begins in 414; the page has the Alans settle in Lusitania and Carthaginensis 'around 409'.

land.text: the Hasdingi kingdom in Gallaecia, whose king Gunderic accepted the Alan crown

successors.note: The people and the crown, not the land: 'most surviving Alans appealed to Gunderic, who accepted them' (Gunderic page); Gunderic is then 'King of Vandals and Alans (418-428)' and Gaiseric 'king of the Vandals and Alans'. Most Alans went to Africa with the Vandals (428 or 429).

land.text: the Alan lands in Lusitania and Carthaginensis

successors.note: The pages say nothing of who held the Alan lands after 418 (confidence 1); a Roman province in law.

correction.text: Lusitania and Carthaginensis, where Respendial's Alans settled

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page has the Alans cross the Rhine on 31 December 406 with the Vandals and Suebi, then 'Around 409 the Alans joined the Vandals and Suebi in crossing the Pyrenees. The Alans led by Respendial settled in Lusitania and Carthaginensis.' Cliopatria's Alan shape (225,102 km2, bbox -9.6 to 0.1 E, 36.9 to 41.5 N) is read as that settlement and brought forward to 409; the year is the page's 'around 409', no month. fx-35 (1 Nov 2026), overlap check: this shape (842 cells) shares 690 cells with the maximus-usurper keyframes _409 and _411 and its found event (Hispania without Gallaecia and Baetica). Vandals page: 'On October 13, 409, they crossed the Pyrenees' and 'the Alans got lands in Lusitania (West) and the region around Carthago Nova'; Kingdom of the Suebi page (cited in maximus-usurper): in 411 'the Alans were allotted the provinces of Lusitania and Hispania Carthaginensis'. No page puts Maximus (the Tarraco court, north-eastern Hispania) in those provinces, so the shape is kept and the overlap belongs to the Maximus dossier (handoff to subtract the Alan land from maximus-usurper_409, _411 and its found region); the size rule already leaves the cells with the Alans.

225,102 km2: Lusitania (93,000 km2 of it, 'Lusitania (Alentejo)' on the page) plus Baetica's northern edge (38,000 km2) and the Carthaginensis plateau (about 100,000 km2). The page: 'In Hispania, the Alans held Lusitania (Alentejo) and Carthaginensis.' No infobox area; the shape is a settlement zone, not a surveyed border.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid for 417-418 only: the Alan lands while the Visigoths destroy them

keyframe_review.note: 225,366 km2 for 417-425. The Alan kingdom ends with its king: 'the Visigoths killed Alan king Attaces in battle in 418 (or 426, according to some authors)' (Alans page); 'The Alans joined in 418. After their king Attaces fell in battle against the Visigoths in Hispania, most surviving Alans appealed to Gunderic, who accepted them' (Gunderic page). So the shape holds for 417-418 only; 419-425 have no Alan territory. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 417..418 from this entry's own 'valid for 417-418 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: no separate Alan shape after 418: the Alans are inside the Vandal shape (Baetica to 428; 'In 428 CE, the Vandals and Alans crossed the Strait of Gibraltar'), then in Africa

keyframe_review.note: 217,937 km2 for 426-438, but 'Respendial's Alans then lost their separate ethnic identity' and 'Most of these Alans went to North Africa with the Vandals'; Gunderic and then Gaiseric were 'King of the Vandals and Alans'. The Alans have no territory of their own after 418: the people ride inside the Vandals' shape (Baetica to 428, then Mauretania and Numidia).

region.text: Lusitania and Carthaginensis, where Respendial's Alans settled

ledger.note: 409: the Alans settle in Hispania. The Alans crossed the Rhine with the Vandals and Suebi on 31 December 406 (Respendial helped the Vandals against the Franks); 'Around 409 the Alans joined the Vandals and Suebi in crossing the Pyrenees', and 'The Alans led by Respendial settled in Lusitania and Carthaginensis.' The year is the page's 'around'; the extent is Cliopatria's 414 shape.

region.text: the Alan lands in Lusitania and Carthaginensis

ledger.note: 418: the Alan lands lapse. The page says nothing of who held Lusitania and Carthaginensis after Attaces fell; they are Roman provinces.

418: the Alan survivors accept Gunderic. 'The Alans joined in 418. After their king Attaces fell in battle against the Visigoths in Hispania, most surviving Alans appealed to Gunderic, who accepted them'; he is 'King of Vandals and Alans (418-428)'. The Alans page gives no date for the submission.

region.text: the Alan lands in Lusitania and Carthaginensis

ledger.note: 418: the Visigoths kill the Alan king Attaces. 'the Visigoths killed Alan king Attaces in battle in 418 (or 426, according to some authors)'; the Alans 'lost their separate ethnic identity'.

wars.name: Visigothic campaign against the Alans in Hispania
wars.outcome: The Visigoths, as Roman federates, killed the Alan king Attaces in battle; the survivors appealed to Gunderic's Vandals.
wars.note: The Alans page gives 418 'or 426, according to some authors'; the campaign proper is dated 417-418 on the Wallia page (see visigoths).

certainty.note: A settlement zone of a people on the move, not a border: no page gives a boundary for Lusitania and Carthaginensis.

notes:
Cliopatria's Alans row (414-438, three shapes) is one settlement zone (Lusitania and Carthaginensis, about 225,000 km2) drawn for 25 years. The pages end the Alan kingdom in 418 with Attaces's death and the submission to Gunderic; so alans_414 is ok, alans_417 holds for 417-418, alans_426 is wrong (the Alans are inside the Vandal shape, then in Africa), and a keyframe is added for 409-413. The dossier starts in 409 (Alans page, 'around 409'), not 414. Family 'steppe' follows alania.
Not in this dossier: (0) the Rhine crossing of 31 December 406 (a war of the vandals dossier; before this dossier's life); (1) the Alans of Gaul: Goar crossed the Rhine in 406 and 'joined the Romans and settled in Gaul'; Aetius settled Goar's people in the Orléanais in 442, 'Goar moved his capital to Orléans', Sangiban held it against Attila, and the page has the Alans of Orléans beat the Goths at Orléans in 463 and Childeric's Franks in 466 (Alans page): a separate state (suggested slug alans-of-orleans, about 442-470s) that Cliopatria lacks, for the additions batch eu-06-x; (2) the Alans of the Caucasus (alania). The pages disagree on the year of Attaces's death (418, or 426 'according to some authors'), on the Strait crossing (428 or 429) and on the submission (418 on the Gunderic page; 419 on the Silingi page, which the vandals dossier uses for the Silingi). The Alans page names the king Attaces, not Addax (the Wallia page's spelling used in visigoths). Gazetteer: 'Carthaginensis' (Hispania Carthaginensis) is missing; the dossier uses Cliopatria's shape instead. Budget: two pages (Alans, Gunderic).
